name: Leninism
summary: Leninism is Vladimir Lenin's adaptation of Marxism: a disciplined vanguard party of committed revolutionaries leads the working class to overthrow the capitalist state and establish a dictatorship of the proletariat through soviets. It adds a theory of imperialism as the monopoly stage of capitalism, support for national self-determination, and a strict secular line towards religion, with the state expected eventually to wither away.
scope: Lenin's own thought and practice from What Is To Be Done? (1902) to his death in 1924, drawing on The State and Revolution, Imperialism and his writings on nations and religion, including war communism and the NEP. It excludes Stalin's later codification (see marxism-leninism), Trotskyism and Maoism.

abolish-armed-forces.rationale: Lenin wanted the standing army replaced by the armed people, not no force at all, since the proletarian state must defend itself.

abolish-central-banks.rationale: The April Theses demand the immediate union of all banks into a single national bank controlled by the Soviet of Workers' Deputies.

abolish-division-of-labor.rationale: Lenin looked to the end of the division between mental and physical labour in the higher phase.

abolish-wage-labour.rationale: Lenin sought to free humanity from wage slavery by suppressing the capitalists, ending wage labour in the higher phase of communism.

alienated-labor.rationale: Wage slavery and the separation of workers from the product of their labour are core Marxist themes Lenin takes over, though he rarely uses the term alienation.

apostasy-punishable.rationale: Lenin endorsed Engels' formula that religion is a purely private matter in relation to the state, so the state may not punish leaving a faith.

basic-income.rationale: In the first phase of communism reward follows labour, so unconditional income is rejected.

bound-labor.rationale: Stalin's account of Leninism describes the peasant revolution as a struggle against the survivals of serfdom and the unlimited power of the landlord.

bypass-parties-groups.rationale: Lenin made the vanguard party the central instrument of revolution, and the Commune model he praised gave power to recallable delegates, not to a leader bypassing parties.

capitalism-causes-war.rationale: The April Theses stress the inseparable connection between capital and the imperialist war and say that without overthrowing capital no truly democratic peace is possible.

capitalism-progressive.rationale: In The Tax in Kind Lenin argued that capitalism is not simply a bane, since compared with patriarchal small production it would be a step forward.

central-bank-independence.rationale: Banks are to be merged into one state syndicate under workers' control, not left independent of the state.

central-planning.rationale: Lenin's programme looked to a planned economy, with Gosplan under Lenin and war communism, though the NEP loosened it.

character-from-environment.rationale: Marxism holds that social being determines consciousness, and Lenin expected the habits of the old order to be remade by new conditions after revolution.

class-collaboration.rationale: Lenin held that spontaneity and cooperation with the bourgeoisie subordinate workers.

class-struggle-history.rationale: Class struggle is the central driver of history in the Marxist framework Lenin adopted.

class-struggle-under-socialism.rationale: The Proletarian Revolution and the Renegade Kautsky holds that the dictatorship of the proletariat continues the class struggle in new forms.

clerical-rule.rationale: Lenin endorsed Engels' formula that religion is a purely private matter in relation to the state, which excludes rule by senior clergy.

competition-drives-progress.rationale: State and Revolution makes class struggle, not competition among peoples, the motor of history.

constituent-assembly.rationale: State and Revolution and The Proletarian Revolution and the Renegade Kautsky hold the Soviet republic to be a higher form of democracy than the Constituent Assembly.

cooperative-communities.rationale: State and Revolution centres on a centralised proletarian state and a single economy-wide syndicate, not on small self-governing communities.

creationism-in-schools.rationale: Lenin endorsed Engels' formula that religion is a purely private matter in relation to the state, so public schools teaching a religious doctrine would contradict it.

defeat-communism.rationale: Lenin's whole programme was to build communism; the statement is the opposite of his position.

defeat-own-government-war.rationale: The April Theses reject the slightest concession to revolutionary defencism in the predatory imperialist war and call for fraternisation at the front.

democracy-best.rationale: Lenin called democracy only one stage on the road to communism and criticized bourgeois democracy.

democracy-is-procedure.rationale: Lenin held that bourgeois democracy is a dictatorship of the capitalist class, so free elections alone do not make a government democratic.

dictatorship-of-proletariat.rationale: Lenin held that the workers hold power and suppress exploiters through the transition until classes vanish.

direct-action.rationale: Lenin argued that communists must take part in bourgeois parliaments and condemned boycotts of elections as an error.

distribute-by-need.rationale: Lenin endorsed from each according to ability, to each according to needs for the higher phase.

divine-source-of-authority.rationale: Lenin held that the state is an organ of class rule and that religion is a private matter in relation to it, so authority is not derived from God.

divinely-chosen-superior-people.rationale: Lenin called religion an opium that stupefies the people and held that the party must fight it, which excludes the claim that God chose a superior people.

dynastic-succession.rationale: The April Theses call for a republic of Soviets with all officials elective and displaceable at any time, which excludes hereditary succession of rulers.

elective-rulers.rationale: State and Revolution calls for elected, recallable officials in place of hereditary or bureaucratic rulers.

emergency-suspend-protections.rationale: The dictatorship of the proletariat is explicitly the suppression of the exploiters by force, free of bourgeois legal limits.

equal-moral-worth.rationale: The Proletarian Revolution and the Renegade Kautsky denies that equality between exploiter and exploited can exist under the dictatorship, while State and Revolution treats equality of right as a formal bourgeois right.

equal-outcomes.rationale: Lenin aimed to end classes and move to distribution by need, though the first phase keeps inequality by labour.

experts-over-public.rationale: Lenin argued that administration is simple enough for any literate worker and that experts should serve the workers.

gradual-change.rationale: Lenin held that the bourgeois state must be smashed by revolution, not reformed.

harm-principle.rationale: Lenin held that the workers' state may restrict exploiters' rights as class measures.

head-commands-forces.rationale: The State and Revolution replaces the standing army with the armed people and makes officials elected and recallable, the opposite of one-man command.

homestead-ownership.rationale: The April Theses call for nationalisation of all lands in the country, which excludes ownership of land by whoever first uses it.

income-for-work-not-ownership.rationale: The State and Revolution describes a first stage of communism in which each is paid according to labour and the parasitic income of owners ends.

independent-unions.rationale: Left-Wing Communism describes the unions' leading bodies as directed by the Communist Party in Soviet Russia, formally non-party.

indirect-election.rationale: The soviet system builds higher bodies from delegates of lower councils, which Lenin favoured as against bourgeois parliaments.

individual-rights-only.rationale: Leninism treats nations as holders of the right to secede and exist as states, so it does not confine rights to individuals.

industrial-civilization-disaster.rationale: Lenin built on industry and productive growth as the basis of communism.

industrial-unions.rationale: Lenin expected trade unions to develop into broader industrial unions embracing whole industries instead of single crafts.

informal-organisation.rationale: What Is To Be Done? argues for a tight, centralised organisation of professional revolutionaries and ridicules the primitive circle methods of the Economists.

interfaith-marriage-restriction.rationale: Lenin endorsed Engels' formula that religion is a purely private matter in relation to the state, which excludes state restrictions on marriage between members of different religions.

labor-aristocracy.rationale: Left-Wing Communism describes an upper stratum of workers in Britain, a semi-petty-bourgeois labour aristocracy, rather than the whole working class in the rich countries.

land-redistribution.rationale: The April Theses demand confiscation of all landed estates and nationalisation of all land, to be disposed of by local Soviets of Agricultural Labourers' and Peasants' Deputies.

laws-from-scripture.rationale: Lenin endorsed Engels' formula that religion is a purely private matter in relation to the state, which leaves no place for laws founded on scripture.

market-under-party-rule.rationale: In The Tax in Kind Lenin defended free trade in peasant produce and state capitalism under proletarian power as the route towards socialism.

markets-allocate-better.rationale: In The Tax in Kind Lenin allowed freedom of trade only as an unavoidable concession that revives capitalism and the petty bourgeoisie, to be held in check by the state-controlled shell of state capitalism.

material-conditions-drive-history.rationale: Historical materialism is the core of Marxism-Leninism; the phases of communism depend on the development of the productive forces.

means-match-ends.rationale: Lenin defended a dictatorship and coercion as means to a stateless society.

military-guardian-role.rationale: Lenin replaces the standing army with the armed people under proletarian control, not a guardian army.

minority-veto.rationale: Stalin's account of Leninism requires subordination of the minority to the majority and practical decisions binding on all members of the party.

mixed-constitution.rationale: Lenin rejected balancing classes in government and called for rule by the working class through soviets alone.

monarchy-legitimate.rationale: The April Theses reject a return to a parliamentary republic for a republic of Soviets from top to bottom with all officials elective and displaceable at any time, which leaves no place for a hereditary monarch.

more-religion-public.rationale: Lenin endorsed Engels' formula that religion is a purely private matter in relation to the state, and the party fights the opium of religion, so religion is to have no public role in the state.

municipal-property.rationale: Lenin wanted production owned by the whole workers' state and organised centrally, not by localities; he criticised syndicalist and decentralist ownership.

nation-first.rationale: The account of Leninism's national question holds that no nation can be free if it oppresses others, and trains workers of ruling nations in true internationalism.

national-church-status.rationale: Lenin endorsed Engels' formula that religion is a purely private matter in relation to the state, which excludes any privileged legal status for a national church.

national-self-determination.rationale: The Foundations of Leninism presents Lenin's principle as the right of nations to independent existence as states, used to expose imperialist annexation.

natural-rulers.rationale: Lenin held that ordinary workers can administer the state, although he also gave a leading role to the vanguard.

neither-capitalism-nor-communism.rationale: Lenin judged the Soviet economy as a transition between capitalism and socialism and expected communism, so he held neither to be unsound.

never-kill-self-defence.rationale: Lenin holds that the old state must be smashed by force and defends revolutionary violence, so no pacifist bar on killing is accepted.

night-watchman-state.rationale: Lenin wanted a state running the whole economy in transition.

no-denominational-politics.rationale: Lenin endorsed Engels' formula that religion is a purely private matter in relation to the state and held that the party must fight religion, which excludes politics organised along denominations.

no-religion-state-schools.rationale: Lenin endorsed Engels' formula that religion is a purely private matter in relation to the state, so the state's schools are not to provide religious instruction.

no-transition-to-communism.rationale: State and Revolution insists on a whole political transition period of proletarian dictatorship and a lower phase of communism before the higher one.

office-by-exam.rationale: Lenin wanted officials elected, paid a workman's wage and recallable, not a separate examined bureaucracy, though he accepted using specialists under workers' control.

offices-by-lottery.rationale: Lenin wanted officials elected and recallable at a workman's wage, not chosen by chance.

one-party-rule.rationale: The party leads the dictatorship of the proletariat and the Bolsheviks banned rivals in 1921, though Lenin did not call one-party rule inherent.

organic-representation.rationale: Lenin wanted soviets of workers, not representation of family and corporate bodies.

parliament-supreme.rationale: Lenin wanted the parliamentary state smashed and replaced by soviets, so he would not endorse parliamentary supremacy.

parliamentary-road-socialism.rationale: Lenin held that the bourgeois state machine must be smashed rather than taken over by parliamentary majorities, and attacked Kautsky for treating parliamentary democracy as the road.

participatory-democracy.rationale: State and Revolution wants all working people to learn to administer the state through soviets, though under a vanguard party.

party-discipline-binding.rationale: Stalin's account of Leninism requires subordination of the minority to the majority and decisions binding on all party members.

people-in-arms.rationale: The State and Revolution calls for replacing the standing army with the armed people.

personal-loyalty-rule.rationale: Lenin's party rested on programme and discipline, not personal oaths.

personal-possessions-private.rationale: State and Revolution takes expropriation to apply to the means of production and keeps distribution of consumption goods by labour in the first phase.

political-elite-corrupt.rationale: Lenin held that parliamentary representatives serve the oppressing class and that officials should lose privileges.

positive-liberty.rationale: Lenin dismissed bourgeois freedom as formal and tied real freedom to material conditions.

press-owned-by-wealth.rationale: Lenin argued that in bourgeois republics the press and meeting-halls belong to capital, so freedom of the press and assembly is formal for the working poor.

private-courts-defense.rationale: Lenin wanted a workers' state that holds the monopoly of force.

production-for-use.rationale: State and Revolution describes communism's higher phase as distribution according to need under common ownership of the means of production.

profit-exploitation.rationale: State and Revolution describes the capitalists as exploiters of wage slaves whom the proletarian dictatorship must suppress to free humanity from wage slavery.

promulgated-standing-laws.rationale: Lenin defined revolutionary dictatorship as rule won and maintained by violence and unrestricted by any laws.

property-franchise.rationale: Soviet suffrage barred property owners and exploiters rather than favouring them; Lenin held that property-based rule is the core of bourgeois dictatorship.

property-fundamental.rationale: Private ownership of the means of production is the root of exploitation and is to be abolished.

public-ownership.rationale: Lenin envisaged the whole economy run as a single state syndicate, and war communism nationalized industry.

punish-blasphemy.rationale: Lenin endorsed Engels' formula that religion is a purely private matter in relation to the state, so the state has no business punishing blasphemy.

reason-over-faith.rationale: Lenin held that a revolutionary party must wage a struggle against the opium of religion which stupefies the people.

recall-officials.rationale: The State and Revolution calls for all officials to be elected and subject to recall at any time.

recallable-delegates.rationale: Lenin's State and Revolution praises the Commune principle that delegates are removable at any time and bound by their electors.

religion-illusion.rationale: Lenin described religion as an opium that stupefies the people, which the party must fight.

religions-one-truth.rationale: Lenin called religion an opium that stupefies the people, which does not fit the claim that all religions express one truth.

religious-equal-recognition.rationale: Lenin endorsed Engels' formula that religion is a purely private matter in relation to the state, so the state gives no confession legal precedence.

religious-nation.rationale: Lenin endorsed Engels' formula that religion is a purely private matter in relation to the state, which excludes defining the national community by religion.

representatives-worker-pay.rationale: Lenin's account of the Commune says all public service should be done at workmen's wages, and The State and Revolution endorses it.

restore-past-order.rationale: Lenin was a revolutionary aiming at a new order.

results-over-ideology.rationale: Lenin held that there can be no revolutionary movement without revolutionary theory.

return-to-foraging.rationale: Lenin's communism required developed productive forces.

right-to-secede.rationale: Stalin's 1924 account of Leninism defines self-determination as the right of oppressed peoples to complete secession and to independent existence as states.

sacred-ruler.rationale: Lenin's State and Revolution treats the state as an organ of class rule and religion as a private matter in relation to it, excluding a sacred ruler.

scripture-inerrant.rationale: Lenin called religion an opium that stupefies the people, and the party struggles against it, which contradicts treating scripture as God's error-free word.

second-chamber.rationale: The State and Revolution rejects bourgeois parliamentarism and calls for working bodies that both legislate and execute, so a separate upper house has no place.

self-interest-moral.rationale: State and Revolution looks to communism where people observe elementary rules of social life by habit, not by pursuing private advantage, and criticises bourgeois wage slavery.

separate-church-state.rationale: State and Revolution quotes and endorses the principle that in relation to the state religion is a purely private matter.

separated-powers.rationale: Lenin wanted a working, not parliamentary, body combining legislation and execution.

smash-state-machine.rationale: Lenin's The State and Revolution argues that the bourgeois state machine must be smashed rather than taken over.

social-market-economy.rationale: The Tax in Kind treats the market and state capitalism as a retreat on the road to socialism, not as a goal of a market economy with a safety net.

socialism-needs-workers-power.rationale: The State and Revolution makes the armed working class, organised through soviets, the ruler of the transitional state, and treats this as the content of socialism.

socialized-markets.rationale: Lenin pictured the whole economy as one state syndicate under a planned system, not a market of separate worker-owned firms, and he treated NEP markets as a retreat.

soviet-state-capitalist.rationale: Lenin said state capitalism would be a step forward for Soviet Russia and that the Soviet state differs economically from the bourgeois state, so his texts point both ways.

state-class-instrument.rationale: Lenin held that the state is an organ of one class's rule over another.

state-harmful.rationale: The state is an instrument of class oppression that will wither away, but it is needed in the transition, so adherents do not call it simply unnecessary.

state-promotes-atheism.rationale: Engels' formula, endorsed by Lenin, makes religion private in relation to the state but not in relation to the party, which wages the struggle against religion itself.

suppress-opposition.rationale: The Proletarian Revolution and the Renegade Kautsky defends dictatorship as rule based directly upon force against the bourgeoisie, which suppresses opposition.

taxation-theft.rationale: The state taxes to fund the common economy; Lenin saw property, not taxation, as exploitation.

unions-good.rationale: Lenin insisted that communists must work inside even reactionary trade unions, because they are the mass organisations of the working class.

unions-run-economy.rationale: Lenin held that unions should join in administration and in training for socialism, while the dictatorship of the proletariat is exercised through the party and the Soviets.

unreligious-rulers-fought.rationale: Lenin endorsed Engels' formula that religion is a purely private matter in relation to the state, which excludes armed overthrow of rulers for not governing under religious law.

vanguard-party.rationale: What Is To Be Done? argues workers left alone reach only trade-union consciousness, so a vanguard party must bring socialist consciousness.

wealth-concentration-endangers-liberty.rationale: State and Revolution says democracy under capitalism stays freedom for the slave-owners and money-bags, since wage slaves are too crushed by want to take part in politics.

widespread-small-property.rationale: Lenin wanted socialized production, not a wide spread of small owners.

withdraw-from-politics.rationale: What Is To Be Done? demands full-time political commitment from revolutionaries.

work-for-welfare.rationale: In the first phase reward follows labour: those who do not work do not eat.

worker-farmer-alliance.rationale: The Tax in Kind aims to strengthen the alliance between workers and peasants and consolidate the dictatorship of the proletariat.

worker-ownership.rationale: Lenin wanted the means of production owned by the whole workers' state, not by each workforce, and opposed syndicalism.

workers-councils.rationale: Lenin held that soviets of workers should hold power instead of a parliament.

workers-nation.rationale: The Foundations of Leninism calls on workers of the ruling nations to support the oppressed peoples' struggle against their own governments, putting internationalism above national solidarity.

workers-own-party.rationale: What Is To Be Done? and Lenin's practice call for a working-class party independent of bourgeois parties.

missingStatements.text: The working class will not reach revolutionary politics on its own; it needs a disciplined party of committed revolutionaries to lead it.
missingStatements.rationale: What Is To Be Done? argues that workers left to themselves develop only trade-union consciousness, so socialist consciousness must be brought from outside by a vanguard.

notes: Second pass (2026-11-15), brought up to rules 7. Every earlier answer was rechecked against the rules: answers that rested on a general value or a guess about Lenin's likely view were nulled, with the earlier version kept in reviewHistory, and answers that Lenin's own texts settle were added or corrected. Sources are Lenin's works from the Marxists Internet Archive (State and Revolution, What Is To Be Done?, Imperialism, the national-question essays, the 1917 draft party programme, the Decree on Peace, the Decree on Land, the dissolution of the Constituent Assembly, the Tax in Kind, the last articles of 1923 and others), saved in scratchpad/sources/leninism/. Themes searched: economy and taxation, property and land, planning and markets, the state and soviet institutions, parties, unions and discipline, the Constituent Assembly and parliaments, religion and schools, nations and self-determination, imperialism and war, women and the family, immigration, abortion and population, press and speech, the army, the courts, culture and morality, agriculture and cooperatives. Most of the statements on technology, ecology, sexuality, criminal justice, monetary policy detail and later political debates are absent from Lenin's texts and stay null. Adherents differ on whether one-party rule and the ban on factions were wartime necessities or part of the doctrine; this profile follows Lenin's own statements and the 1917-1922 practice, and does not treat Stalin's later codification as Leninism. No source in the library records the Soviet press, army-commissar or party-ban measures as acts, so those statements stay null here. Wikipedia (s1) is cited only for the overview and never as the sole evidence for an answer.

keyFigures.role: Founder and main theorist of Leninism, leader of the Bolsheviks
keyFigures.quote: Leninism is a political theory and practice developed by Vladimir Lenin, adapting Marxism to early 20th-century Russia.
